drafts.title: Reference checks that actually tell you something
drafts.excerpt: Most reference checks are a box-ticking waste of time. The questions that actually surface the truth — and how to read what’s not said.
prompts: Candid, documentary-style photo that looks like a real, unposed moment snapped on a phone by a colleague — NOT a staged, glossy or stock shot. Scene: a hiring manager at his desk on a phone call, phone to his ear and pen paused over a notepad of scribbled notes, listening carefully with a slightly reading-between-the-lines expression. Real, ordinary Singaporean people with natural, unforced expressions; nobody looking at or aware of the camera; a genuine, lived-in setting with a little authentic clutter. Soft natural light, slightly imperfect off-centre framing, subtle film grain, real skin and textures, no beautifying or retouching. Landscape 16:9 (~1600x900). No text, no logos, no watermark, no readable signage.
